title: Introductory rollout playbook for non-ops teams (wip)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, non-ops-centric playbook to help product managers, PM-led engineers, and design partners understand how to plan and execute an LLM feature rollout (canary / A/B) without getting lost in deep SRE runbooks. Intended as the first checklist you share with stakeholder groups before involving full ops.

Audience:
- PMs launching conversational or generative features
- Feature engineers who don’t own SRE oncall
- Product designers running user-facing experiments
- Solutions/CS who coordinate pilot customers

When to use this doc:
- You have a model change, prompt redesign, or new retriever / reranker and want staged exposure.
- You expect non-trivial latency/cost changes or user-visible behavior shifts.
- You need to coordinate SLOs, fallback, and human gating but don’t want to require deep SRE changes for early pilots.

Quick 8-step checklist (non-ops fast path):
1) Scope & hypothesis (PM): write 1-sentence hypothesis + primary metric (e.g., increase NPS on search answer by +4 points). Keep it simple.
2) Safety & impact triage (PM + Trust): identify content moderation risk and whether legal/compliance review required. If yes, stop and loop in security.
3) Ask SRE for minimal telemetry (see telemetry section). Copy paste the telemetry snippet in the Slack channel.
4) Define fallback behavior: percentage rollback, serve-old-model route, or feature flag off. Prefer automated flag if available.
5) Pick cohort slice (product): choose 1–2 small, well-defined cohorts (e.g., internal beta, 1% US web traffic). Capture cohort definition in doc.
6) Dry-run smoke tests (engineering + QA): run synthetic traffic test and 50 user-interaction manual checks.
7) Launch pilot (PM signals): open Slack #rollouts with 1-line start message, include runbook link and oncall contact.
8) Observe & decide (24–72h): collect telemetry and scoped qualitative feedback. Decide: ramp / hold / rollback. Log decision.

Minimum telemetry to request from SRE (copy/paste):
- 95th/99th p50/p90 latency per route (ms)
- Token/sec and tokens per request (avg/95th)
- Errors by class (timeout, model-error, service-5xx)
- Cost delta estimate per 24h (approx)
- Success-rate for function/tool calls (if used)
- Key safety signals: content filter hits, unsafe completions count

Easy telemetry message (paste to #sre-requests):
"Hi SRE — pilot request for feature X. Minimum telemetry needed: latency p50/p95, token usage, error classes, cost delta, and filter hits. Pilot cohort: internal beta (account IDs: ...). Desired retention window: 7 days. Contact: @AveryChen. JIRA: JIRA-4567. Thanks!"

Human gates (how a non-ops PM can gate progress):
- Gate 1 (smoke): manual approval after dry-run + 0 critical errors in 1h of synthetic traffic.
- Gate 2 (observability): no >2% increase in error-rate and latency within SLO for 24h on pilot traffic.
- Gate 3 (qualitative): product owners review 30 flagged examples and approve behaviour.

Fallback options (non-ops-friendly):
- Feature flag toggle (preferred): immediate off via UI or chatops.
- Route shadowing: divert to old model for a percentage of requests. Works when routing is simple.
- Client-side guardrail: reduce request size or disable optional re-ranker on degradation.

Quick comms templates (PM -> stakeholders):
- Slack start (short): "Launching pilot for feature X to internal beta (1% traffic). Hypothesis: ... Oncall: @sre-rotation. Link: <doc>. Will monitor for 48h and post decision."
- Slack rollback: "Rolling back feature X for all cohorts due to increased 95th latency > SLO. Rolling to old-model route. Investigating root cause. Triage board: <link>."

Decision logging: what to record after each gate
- who decided (name), time, metric snapshots (latency, errors, cost delta), qualitative notes (3 examples), next steps. Save one-line summary in rollout doc and ping #rollouts.

Simple experiment design primer for PMs (A/B basics):
- Unit: user session or request? Prefer session for chat features to avoid leakage across messages.
- Size: start with small percentages, increase in powers of two (1% -> 2% -> 4% ...), evaluate after each hold period.
- Stopping rule: primary metric confidence interval crosses zero or negative impact beyond tolerance.

Glossary (short):
- Canary = small, time-bound exposure to production traffic.
- A/B = randomized assignment with a control group.
- Cohort = explicitly defined user subset (by ID, region, or account).
- Human gate = manual approval checkpoint.

Common pitfalls (notes to self):
- Starting with too broad a cohort ("all users") — avoid.
- No easy rollback path — make rollback first class.
- Neglecting token-cost monitoring; surprise bills happen fast.
- Running A/B on multi-turn chat without session-level bucketing causes contamination.

Lightweight QA checklist (engineers):
- Confirm model version pinning and route mapping.
- Sanity prompts (10), edge-case prompts (10), and filter-trigger tests (5).
- Verify function/tool mocks if integrated.
- Confirm logs contain session_id and cohort_tag.

Comms and escalation chain (keep small):
- PM -> SRE duty -> SRE lead -> Product lead -> Trust/legal (if needed).
- For unsafe content policy violations escalate immediately to Trust and pause pilot.

Templates: observation table (paste into doc)
- timestamp | cohort | p95 latency | errors% | cost delta | notes
- 2024-12-02T08:12Z | internal-beta | 210ms | 0.1% | +12% | two stale retriever hits

Open questions (needs decisions):
- What is the default ramp cadence? (24h vs 72h) — recommend 48h unless cost/latency sensitive.
- Who signs the final rollback authority for cross-team launches? Product manager can do pilot-level rollback; enterprise-facing changes require Eng + CS + Legal sign-off.
- Can we standardize a feature-flag template for immediate global rollback? (ask infra/product flags team)

Links & quick refs:
- SRE quick link: #sre-requests (Slack)
- Example experiment doc template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/Experiment+Template
- Quick smoke-run script (repo): github.com/redwood-inference/ops-smoke-scripts

Notes to self (rough):
- This doc should sit alongside the deep ops runbooks, not replace them. Make it the "first read" for non-ops PMs and include a one-click checklist (todo widget) in console later.
- Try running a short internal workshop with PMs and 1 SRE to validate the wording.

Revision history:
- 2024-11-10: initial outline (Avery)
- 2024-11-20: added telemetry snippets and comms templates (Nina)
- 2024-12-03: clarified ramps and human gates (Marcus)

Unresolved items for follow-up (owners in parens):
- Finalize standard ramp cadence (Product ops)
- Feature-flag rollback template (Infra product)
